# SK9018 — The file is not valid in the encoding it declares

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

The file holds bytes its encoding cannot decode — a Latin-1 `é` in a file with no BOM, which is read as UTF-8 — so it is reported and left byte-identical. No verb writes it: not `format`, `arrange`, `fix` or `verify`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Tool |
| Default severity | error |
| Scope | Syntax |
| Needs a compilation | no |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 2.0 |

## Why

#387. The file used to be decoded with U+FFFD for every undecodable byte, formatted, and written back with the original bytes gone. Neither unconditional promise saw it: the token comparison (`SK9099`) runs after the decode, where both sides hold the same U+FFFD, and U+FFFD inside a literal or a comment parses (`SK9010`). The token stream is only as trustworthy as the decode that produced it. It is an error where `SK9010` is a warning because nothing else will flag it: a file that does not parse fails the build, while a Latin-1 file compiles with zero warnings — `csc` decodes the bad byte as U+FFFD too, measured on SDK 10.0.401 — so a warning would let `format --check` and `verify` pass over a file Skala has never checked. Re-save the file as UTF-8 and it is formatted like any other.

## When it does not fire

None; the bytes either decode strictly in the encoding the file's byte-order mark declares (UTF-8 without one) or they do not. UTF-8 with or without a BOM and UTF-16 or UTF-32 with a BOM are read as before. UTF-16 without a BOM is read as UTF-8: an ASCII-only one decodes and is `SK9010` on its NULs, as it always was; one holding any character above U+007F is not valid UTF-8 and is this.
